root_idea.summary: A root centered on the winter season, the time opposed to summer.
root_idea.development: The seasonal noun extends in Classical Arabic to expressions for entering or being affected by winter, remaining in a place during winter, winter weather and hardship, winter-related terms, and places or periods associated with wintering.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Canonical Quranic noun displayed under the normalized citation form شِتَاءٌ.

senses.usage_conditions: In Qur'an 106:2, it occurs in the expression “the journey of winter and summer,” naming the season opposed to summer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To commence, or begin, as winter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive seasonal verb describing the onset of winter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become intensely cold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested with a day as subject, as in “the day became intensely cold.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remain, stay, dwell, or abide in a place during winter; to winter in a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a place, country, or town; the same construction is also attested for pasturing cattle there during winter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To experience drought, barrenness, or dearth during winter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A seasonal hardship usage applied to a people or group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be smitten or affected by winter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct stative verb describing the effect of winter on a subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suffice or provide enough for one's winter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction “this thing will suffice me for my winter.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bargain for or arrange work by the winter season; in the related construction, to hire or take someone as a hireling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional Form III seasonal-work expression, with شِتَاءً functioning as a verbal noun rather than merely an adverb of time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter the winter season.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form IV verb is attested of people entering winter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rough or rugged place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal geographic usage distinct from the seasonal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The higher, upper, front, or fore part of a valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographic term for a particular part of a valley.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pertaining or relating to winter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational adjective with variant formations associated with شِتَاءٌ and شَتْوَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Winter rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized seasonal-weather usage of the relational form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Seasonal increase or offspring among sheep and goats, and similarly a young camel born in the relevant seasonal cycle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized livestock term; the cited account associates it with a named seasonal birth cycle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In calendrical reckoning, a seasonal quarter or one of the six two-month seasons; in another reckoning, the half-year beginning at the autumnal equinox.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited calendar classifications vary; this is an extended temporal usage beyond the ordinary designation of winter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hail falling from the sky.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct noun usage glossed as بَرَدٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Drought or dearth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A seasonal usage associated specifically with winter because people remain in tents and do not go out to seek herbage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Entering or being in winter, with winter understood as a season of drought or dearth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival or participial seasonal expression in which the winter period is characterized by scarcity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Intensely cold, or marked by hail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of a day or morning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The winter time, a place of wintering, or wintering considered as an act or verbal noun.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two related forms are explicitly used for the time, place, and source or act associated with wintering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a reported traditional reading, being in straitness, dearth, hunger, and scarcity of milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning belongs to a disputed variant reading in a traditional quotation; the commonly transmitted reading is reported as مُسْنِتُونَ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Remaining or pasturing in a place during winter.
Upper or front part of a valley.
Ordinary winter sense and extended calendrical usages.
Drought or dearth as a winter usage.
Entering winter understood as a season of dearth.
Cold or hail affecting a day or morning.
Place of wintering, with related time and verbal-noun uses covered by the same lexical family.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the seasonal-offspring usage.
Reported traditional reading denoting scarcity and hunger.

cautions: The Quranic sense is the ordinary winter-season meaning; Classical extensions such as hail, drought or dearth, and calendrical periods are listed separately.
The مُشْتٍ scarcity meaning is preserved as a disputed traditional reading, not as an unqualified general usage.
